title: The routing slack: a 6-way linear domain router on the sealed 6144-atom codes
question: How much routing slack does the sealed code carry? Can a 6-way linear domain router fit on the frozen 6144-atom codes identify the domain of a test row, and with what confidence? Prerequisite diagnostic for the M139b assembled buy-back. No kill switch: the buy-back gate lives in M139b.

sealed_codes.note: Reuses the SEALED M117 6144-atom code memmaps. One streaming pass accumulates the Gram and BOTH cross-targets (345-class for the t1 anchor, 6-domain for the router). No encode, CPU-only.

domain_head.note: Closed-form ridge, lambda=1.0, standardised + intercept — the exact RidgeAccumulator convention, same as the class head.

gate.t1_reference: the class head on the same codes reproduces M117 sealed Q(6144,138000) = 0.2248695652173913 (validates codes-to-labels pairing)
gate.no_kill_switch: M139a is a prerequisite diagnostic. The buy-back gate (>= 4/6 domains beat their dense arm at matched cost) lives in M139b.
